summary: André Caquot (1923–2004) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and École Pratique des Hautes Études, he held posts at EPHE, the universities of Strasbourg and Paris, and the Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture (b. 1945) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Laval University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and Paris-Sorbonne University, and held a post at Laval University around 1979.

André Godard (1881–1965) was an archaeologist and historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies who attended the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts. He served with DAFA (1923), the Archaeological Service of Iran (1928–1953), and the University of Tehran (1934–1949).

Linguist André Martinet (1908–1999) studied at ENS, the Sorbonne/University of Paris, and Humboldt University under Joseph Vendryes and Antoine Meillet. His career included posts at EPHE (1938–1946), Columbia University (1947–1955), University of Paris (1955–1969), and Paris Descartes University (1969–1977).
Linguist André Mazon (1881–1967) studied at Charles University and the Faculty of Arts of Paris between 1900 and 1905. He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.
André Oltramare (1822–1896) was Professor of Latin at the University of Geneva from circa 1848 to 1896, where he succeeded Paul Oltramare.

André Padoux (1920–2017) studied Indology and religious studies under Louis Renou, Olivier Lacombe, Georg Morgenstierne, Alf Sommerfelt, Lilian Silburn, and Swami Lakshman Joo. He directed the Institut Français Frankfurt (1953–1959) and served as Directeur de Recherche at the CNRS (1959–1985).

André Wedemeyer (1875–1958) was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctorate under August Conrady around 1905–1912 and held a post at the University of Leipzig from roughly 1920 to 1935.

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Chicago and CIHTS under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins. He holds posts at Smith College and as Foreign Adjunct Professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Anett Krause works in Indology and computational fields. Educated at the universities of Leipzig, Halle-Wittenberg, and Marburg, she held researcher posts at Marburg, Halle-Wittenberg, the Akademie der Wissenschaften Mainz, and a project coordinator post at the Royal Library of Berlin (2023).

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctorate at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and served as a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology who has held posts at the Free University of Berlin and as a researcher at the University of Oulu (attested 1998).

Angela Sumegi is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, studying under Nalini Devdas, and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities (attested 2008).

Angela Zito is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago in 1989. In 1999, she was appointed Associate Professor at New York University, an institution she also helped found.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs studied at Freiburg, New College, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, and Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She taught at Konstanz and Goethe University Frankfurt (1993–2001) before taking the chair of Practical Philosophy at the University of Basel in 2001.

Angelika Malinar (b. 1961) is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies educated at the universities of Mainz and Tübingen. She held teaching posts at SOAS and Free University of Berlin before becoming Professor of Indology at the University of Zurich in 2009.

Angelo Brelich (1913–1977) was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University from roughly 1933 to 1937 and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from circa 1958 to 1977.

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as professor at the Istituto di Studi Superiori di Firenze and Sapienza University of Rome.

Angelo Francesco Saverio Maffei (1844–1899) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Seminario Maggiore Arcivescovile di Trento and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He served as Rector of St Aloysius College (1891–1896) and Fellow at the University of Madras (1895–1899).

Angelo Maria Pizzagalli (1883–1944) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa under Carlo Formichi. He held posts at the University of Pisa (1913), the University of Genoa (1914), and the University of Milan (circa 1924–1944).
